a signed token that proves who is calling the API

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Sign-in token and session file
sections.what: Makes a short signed token for a test admin and writes it, with the base address, to a private temporary file.
sections.why: Likely reason: the browser test needs a signed-in session without a real login.
sections.watch_out: Anyone who reads that file can use the token for 30 minutes.

sections.name: api
sections.title: API calls and checks
sections.what: Defines a helper that calls the Opportunity Map API with the token, then checks counts, branding, private partner names, account links, and optionally refreshes BHP.
sections.why: The checks are the privacy and content acceptance checks for the demo.
sections.watch_out: Partner names are read from the catalog, so a new partner name is checked only after it is added there.

summary: Smoke test that signs in as an admin-style test user, checks the Opportunity Map state for the expected counts and privacy, and optionally triggers a BHP refresh.
purpose: Confirms the Opportunity Map loads with the expected 68 accounts and 30 solutions and does not leak private partner names.
why: The header calls it a local acceptance utility, so it is a manual check, not a unit test.
how: Makes a short-lived signed token, writes it to a temporary browser session file, calls the state endpoint, and checks counts, branding, private partner names and account links. Optionally calls the refresh endpoint.
inputs: The JWT_SECRET or SESSION_SECRET setting, the REPLIT_DEV_DOMAIN setting, and an optional --research flag.
outputs: A one-line PASS summary printed to the console and a session file in /tmp.
risks: Writes a session token to a temporary file, which is a credential. Counts are hard-coded and will fail after any catalog change.
debug: If it fails on counts, check the catalog for the number of accounts and solutions. If it fails on privacy, look for the leaking partner name in the state output.
